subject: Clarify custodian handover, break-glass, and cross-border forensics (Private Deploy)
messages:
From: Aisha Gray <aisha.gray@medscan.health>
To: Dev Patel <dev.patel@redwood.ai>
Cc: Tom Ellis <tom.ellis@medscan.health>, security@medscan.health
Date: Wed, 5 Aug 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Private deploy: custody, break-glass & forensics questions

Hi Dev —

Thanks for the walkthrough yesterday. A couple of follow-ups from our SOC and Legal teams so we can progress the PO:

1) Custodian handover: we need a short, auditable process for handing over customer-managed keys and for inventorying the keystore after initial sync. Who performs the physical import (MedScan vs Redwood ops) for an on-prem package and how is that logged?

2) Break-glass: in an incident where Redwood must perform emergency access to run urgent forensics, what is the policy and which logs will show access (operator id, justification ticket, time window)?

3) Cross-border forensics: if we require third-party forensics (EU-based vendor) can the logs/artifacts be exported to them, and what redaction/support does Redwood offer?

Tom from Legal may add a few contract asks — looping him in. Can we get a short write-up and any diagram you have by end of day Friday?

Appreciate it,
Aisha
Security Manager — MedScan Health

From: Dev Patel <dev.patel@redwood.ai>
To: Aisha Gray <aisha.gray@medscan.health>
Cc: karthik.iyer@redwood.ai, kimberly.park@redwood.ai, jonas.weber@redwood.ai
Date: Wed, 5 Aug 2026 12:03:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Private deploy: custody, break-glass & forensics questions

Aisha —

Thanks for the clear list. Quick answers up front, and I'll attach a short diagram + the DPA annex redline for Legal.

1) Custodian handover: For the on-prem package we support two patterns:
   - Customer-import (preferred): MedScan performs the KMS import. Redwood provides an import script and verification checks. The customer account admin runs the import; the import produces a signed audit bundle (timestamp, public key thumbprint, and import tool logs) that is pushed to the private control plane audit bucket.
   - Assisted-import (opt-in): Redwood SRE assists under an MSA playbook; assistance requires documented POA and is recorded in our operator-access ledger. Assisted imports can only be scheduled and must be approved by your security contact.

2) Break-glass: Redwood's emergency-forensics flow requires:
   - formal request via your security portal or a signed email to security@redwood.ai (we capture the request id),
   - approval from two internal roles (SRE on-call + Security Lead) for assisted actions,
   - operator actions are logged with operator id, ticket id, action scope, and ephemeral session IDs in the operator ledger (immutable append-only entries stored in your private control-plane logging instance).

3) Cross-border forensics: Exports of logs/artifacts are supported. Redwood can:
   - provide redacted bundles (PII tokens masked) on request, or
   - ship a full encrypted archive to a designated vendor key provided by you.

I've attached a one-page diagram (custodian-handover-diagram.v1.png) and our proposed DPA Annex A redline (RDW_DPA_AnnexA_medscan_redline.pdf). Karthik and Kimberly are on copy for any contract specifics. We can refine wording for your Legal.

Best,
Dev Patel
Solutions Engineer — Redwood Inference

From: Kimberly Park <kimberly.park@redwood.ai>
To: Tom Ellis <tom.ellis@medscan.health>, Aisha Gray <aisha.gray@medscan.health>
Cc: Dev Patel <dev.patel@redwood.ai>, karthik.iyer@redwood.ai
Date: Thu, 6 Aug 2026 08:33:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Private deploy: custody, break-glass & forensics questions

Tom / Aisha —

Attaching a few redlines and a suggested contractual paragraph we'd expect in Annex A to satisfy the three asks (see PDF). High-level points we added:

- Assisted import conditions and POA: we define the narrow scope (one-time import, no read-only key export) and require customer-written POA within 48h of scheduled work.
- Emergency access: we added a clause that any emergency operator action will be documented and that customer retains right to a third-party review within 30 days.
- Cross-border: we allow encrypted export to an EU vendor key and require your acceptance of a minimal legal transfer addendum if export is outside your jurisdiction.

We've tried to keep the language tight to limit scope creep. If you prefer the customer-import-only model we can remove assisted-import language.

Kimberly Park
Head of Privacy & Compliance — Redwood Inference

From: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.ai>
To: security@medscan.health, Aisha Gray <aisha.gray@medscan.health>
Cc: Dev Patel <dev.patel@redwood.ai>, kimberly.park@redwood.ai, jonas.weber@redwood.ai
Date: Thu, 6 Aug 2026 14:45:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Private deploy: custody, break-glass & forensics questions

Asha / Security team —

One operational note on logging retention and evidence collection:

- All operator ledger entries are retained inside your private control-plane with default retention of 7 years (configurable).
- Forensics bundles include: timestamped audit log, agent traces for the affected node(s), and a signed manifest referencing the imported key thumbprints.
- If you need continuous forwarding to an on-prem SIEM, we can enable a delivery hook (TLS + mutual TLS auth) so copies are pushed live to your collector — this avoids ad-hoc exports and reduces transfer risk.

Jonas is looping in to confirm SLA language for assisted imports and to propose the fallback if operator access is required but POA/approval channels are unavailable (we recommend short-lived break-glass tokens with out-of-band notification).

Thanks,
Karthik
Head of Infrastructure 

From: Aisha Gray <aisha.gray@medscan.health>
To: Dev Patel <dev.patel@redwood.ai>, kimberly.park@redwood.ai
Cc: Tom Ellis <tom.ellis@medscan.health>, karthik.iyer@redwood.ai
Date: Fri, 7 Aug 2026 16:02:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Private deploy: custody, break-glass & forensics questions

Thanks — this is exactly what we needed. A couple of quick confirmations before we send the PO:

- MedScan will opt for Customer-import only for initial keystore seeding; we'll run import and push the signed audit bundle to the control-plane.
- We want the delivery hook to our on-prem SIEM enabled as part of deployment (TLS mTLS). Can you include the configuration guide in the deployment runbook?
- Legal to review the redline and propose any final tweaks on the assisted-import clause (we'll likely delete it if POA is onerous).

Once Legal signs off we'll cut the PO and target a mid-September install. Appreciate the quick turnaround and the diagram — saved us a call.

— Aisha
